verses.text: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
“That’s why my thoughts are pushing me to answer. I feel the rush to speak.
I’ve heard the rebuke meant to shame me, and my own understanding gives me an answer.
Haven’t you known this from way back, ever since people were put on the earth?
The wicked don’t get to celebrate for long. The joy of the godless lasts a moment.
Even if their greatness climbs to heaven and their head reaches the clouds,
they’ll be gone for good like their own dung. People who saw them will ask, ‘Where’d they go?’
They’ll disappear like a dream, and nobody will find them. They’ll be chased away like a vision in the night.
The eyes that saw them won’t see them again. Even the place they lived won’t see them anymore.
Their children will have to seek the favor of the poor, and their own hands will give back their wealth.
Their bones are full of youthful strength, but that youth will lie down with them in the dust.
“Wickedness may taste sweet in their mouth, and they may hide it under their tongue.
They may savor it and refuse to let it go, keeping it in their mouth.
But once that food reaches their stomach, it turns into cobra venom inside them.
They swallowed riches, but they’ll throw them back up. God will drive those riches out of their belly.
They’ll suck in cobra venom. The viper’s tongue will kill them.
They won’t see rivers or flowing streams of honey and butter.
They’ll give back what they worked for without getting to swallow it down. They won’t enjoy the wealth they’ve gained.
They crushed the poor and left them behind. They seized a house by force and won’t build it up.
“Because they never knew peace inside, they won’t save a thing they took pleasure in.
There was nothing they didn’t gobble up, so their prosperity won’t last.
When they have more than enough, distress will catch up with them. Everyone who’s suffering will turn against them.
Just as they’re about to fill their belly, God will throw his fierce anger at them. It’ll rain down on them while they eat.
They’ll run from the iron weapon, only to be struck through by a bronze arrow.
They pull it out, and it comes out of their body, its shining point drawn from their liver. Terror comes over them.
Total darkness is waiting for their treasures. A fire no one fanned will devour them and burn up whatever’s left in their tent.
The heavens will expose their wrongdoing, and the earth will rise up against them.
The wealth of their household will be swept away, rushing off on the day of God’s anger.
That’s the share God gives the wicked, the inheritance he’s set aside for them.”
